tasks.short: Attend meetings and seminars, gather useful ideas, and report training progress.

steps.what: Choose relevant meetings or seminars from invitations and programme priorities.
Prepare programme figures and questions for the selected event.
Attend the event, ask questions, and share relevant training progress.
Turn event notes into a short account of lessons and open questions.

loop.input: Personal event notes and meeting brief.
loop.output: Learning summary with note references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check every factual statement against supplied notes; specialist checks meaning and confidentiality.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; return notes and a blank template if unsupported statements remain.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation; a template cannot reliably preserve their meaning.

steps.what: Recommend useful follow-ups and send the reviewed summary to management.

tasks.design: A reusable generator combines approved figures from the {LMS} with programme priorities in {DOCS} to prepare a meeting brief. A bounded drafting loop turns personal notes into a source-linked summary in {DOCS}; the specialist reviews it before sharing through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme figures needed manual assembly, and event notes differed widely. Attendance itself depends on live questions and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and templates support deterministic preparation. Bounded drafting can reduce note cleanup without requiring automatic recording.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing worthwhile events and judging whether advice fits the workforce remain difficult. Confidential discussions may not be suitable for model processing.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the question nobody prepared, notice disagreement, and judge which lesson deserves action.

ambition.what: A monthly decision on which training module should be refreshed next.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling figures and cleaning notes, while attendance remains substantial. They can bring monthly refresh recommendations; programme approval rights remain with the training manager.

reach.learn: Compare evidence of skill gaps, operational impact, and the cost of changing a module.

evidence.claim: Structured training figures can populate reusable briefs, while free-text notes benefit from reviewed drafting.
Generated reports require source checks; the digest documents a report containing nonexistent references.

assumptions: Time shares describe a typical blend of seminars and programme status meetings, not a mandatory sequence for every event.
Meetings may be remote or in person; personal notes are sufficient and recording is unnecessary.
GDPR applies to personal data in notes; use restricted access, limited retention, and an established lawful basis.
Build ranges cover one brief template, one notes workflow, and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which programme figures are available from the {LMS}?
Which event notes may be processed and shared?
What access and employee consultation are required under national rules?
research_questions: Does a brief improve preparation enough to justify its maintenance?
Can summaries preserve caveats and distinguish event claims from verified facts?
new_work: Review summaries for unsupported claims and confidential details.
Maintain figure definitions and brief templates.
Fix broken exports and remove obsolete event notes.

tasks.short: Recruit training participants, resolve placement constraints, and enrol approved cohorts.

steps.what: Collect employee requests and manager nominations for planned training.
Check prerequisites and employee details against training and employee records.
Match eligible requests to course capacity and available dates.
Resolve conflicting priorities, release time, and access needs with participants and managers.
Approve participant release time and proposed placements.
Enrol approved participants and issue session details.

tasks.design: Configure request forms, approvals, enrolment, and reminders in the {LMS} or {WORKFLOW}. A deterministic integration checks limited fields from the {HCM} and {LMS}, then proposes cohorts using capacity and availability; people resolve disputed placements before approved enrolments reach the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived in different formats, employee and course records were separate, and release-time decisions lived in mailboxes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment workflows cover much of the task. Small integrations and explicit scheduling constraints can replace manual copying without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Scarce places, shift coverage, accessibility, and contested development opportunities require discussion. Missing prerequisites need correction rather than automatic exclusion.
tasks.human_edge: Make participation workable and fair when operational demands conflict with an employee's development needs.

ambition.what: Offer recurring training cohorts for shift workers using their actual release windows.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time resolving access barriers and less time chasing nominations. They can propose additional cohort times; managers retain release-time approval.

reach.task: Identify barriers to employee access to development.
reach.learn: Handle sensitive access needs, distinguish missing data from ineligibility, and review participation patterns.

evidence.claim: Forms, explicit prerequisite checks, capacity matching, and enrolment approvals can use deterministic workflows.
AI used for worker evaluation or certain employment decisions can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories.
Dutch national rules include works council consent provisions for specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Participants are existing employees; this is course recruitment, not hiring.
The {LMS} supports course capacity, enrolment, and completion records.
Checks flag missing records; they do not rank employee potential or decide career opportunities.
GDPR applies; collect only necessary employee fields and restrict sensitive access information.
Build ranges cover one programme family and include applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which prerequisites and allocation priorities are approved?
Does the {LMS} support forms, approvals, and waiting lists?
How are shift coverage and access needs handled?
Which national rules and consultation procedures apply?
Are employee identifiers consistent between the {HCM} and {LMS}?
research_questions: Can existing configuration cover enrolment before custom integration is needed?
Do proposed cohorts improve shift-worker participation without creating coverage gaps?
new_work: Resolve missing records and disputed eligibility checks.
Review waiting-list fairness and unresolved placements.
Maintain capacity, prerequisite, and scheduling rules.
Monitor enrolment failures and duplicate notifications.

tasks.short: Select suitable instructors, agree availability, and record training assignments.

steps.what: Translate learning objectives and cohort needs into instructor requirements.
Check instructor qualifications, approved rates, and availability.
Compare instructors against required qualifications, dates, language, and budget.
Select an instructor using subject expertise, teaching approach, and cohort fit.
Agree session dates and delivery expectations with the selected instructor.
Record the confirmed assignment and update session invitations.

tasks.design: Generate instructor requirements from a structured training brief in {DOCS}, then join approved instructor records, rates, and availability from the {LMS}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {CALENDAR}. A deterministic shortlist exposes constraints and missing data; the specialist selects the instructor, agrees delivery expectations, and triggers configured assignment updates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructor qualifications, rates, and calendars were maintained separately. Teaching fit was mixed into administrative comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable schemas and small integrations can assemble reliable comparisons quickly. Explicit filters handle administrative requirements without automated teaching-quality scores.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can be stale, and qualifications do not prove teaching quality. New instructors and unusual cohorts need direct assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether an instructor can teach this audience and establish clear expectations before delivery.

ambition.what: Maintain a qualified backup instructor option for critical onboarding sessions.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling shortlists and more time assessing teaching fit and delivery resilience. Selection rights remain within the existing budget and delegation limits.

reach.task: Plan instructor capacity for critical programmes.
reach.learn: Assess coverage risk, teaching quality, and the cost of retaining backup capacity.

evidence.claim: Qualification, availability, and budget constraints support deterministic shortlisting while teaching fit remains a human decision.
AI-based worker evaluation or task allocation can raise EU AI Act high-risk questions depending on purpose.

assumptions: The training brief contains structured objectives, language, delivery mode, and required qualifications.
External instructors already have approved commercial terms; new contracting follows a separate approval process.
The specialist has delegated authority to choose instructors within approved limits.
GDPR applies to instructor records; use limited fields, access controls, and correction procedures.
Build ranges include consultation under national rules where employee assignment or monitoring arrangements change.
unknowns: Where are instructor qualifications and expiry dates recorded?
Which filters are mandatory and which allow exceptions?
Who approves external instructor bookings and additional spend?
What employee consultation is required under national rules?
research_questions: Can the {LMS} already store instructor qualifications and resource availability?
Does a deterministic shortlist retain suitable instructors when records are incomplete?
new_work: Keep instructor qualifications, rates, and availability current.
Resolve missing records and justified filter exceptions.
Check assignment updates and calendar conflicts.
Review backup coverage and instructor feedback.

tasks.short: Negotiate training scope, outcomes, fees, and expenses, then secure an approved contract.

steps.what: Discuss the client's training needs, intended outcomes, and delivery constraints.
Calculate delivery costs, proposed fees, expense limits, and permitted concessions.
Draft contract terms using approved clauses and the proposed delivery scope.

loop.input: Training brief, validated cost proposal, and approved clause library.
loop.output: Draft scope and outcome wording within a deterministically populated agreement.
loop.check: Validate amounts and required clauses mechanically; specialist checks scope, commitments, and source references.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved wording returns to the specialist. Never send automatically.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill prices and standard clauses, but bespoke training outcomes require reviewed free-text drafting.

steps.what: Negotiate outcomes, scope, fees, and expenses within delegated limits.
Review nonstandard clauses and resolve legal or liability concerns.
Approve the final commitments and sign through the authorised signing process.
File the signed agreement and register delivery obligations and billing details.

tasks.design: Configure cost formulas using approved rates from the {ERP}, and populate standard terms in the {CLM}. A bounded loop drafts only bespoke scope wording for review; people negotiate and authorise commitments through {ESIGN}, after which a deterministic integration registers obligations in {PROJECT} and billing details in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope, price assumptions, and contract versions were scattered across documents. Bespoke outcomes and negotiation could not be reduced to templates alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, formulas, approval routes, and signing workflows cover the structured work. Bounded drafting can help with bespoke wording when approved inputs are available.
tasks.still_hard: Outcome commitments, liability, scope changes, and concessions need judgement. Contract integrations are expensive when signed documents do not retain structured fields.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what the client truly values, trade concessions wisely, and avoid promises the training programme cannot deliver.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time rebuilding cost sheets and contract paperwork, with more preparation time for negotiation. Negotiation limits and signing rights do not change.

reach.task: Approve training commitments against workforce priorities and budget.
reach.learn: Define measurable outcomes, understand contract exposure, and distinguish delivery commitments from guaranteed performance gains.

evidence.claim: Cost formulas, standard contract assembly, approval routing, and obligation registration can be deterministic.
Bespoke contract drafting needs source verification and human review before external use.

assumptions: This task applies where the company provides training to external clients; many internal HR teams rarely perform it.
Approved rates, clauses, and delegation limits exist.
Legal review focuses on deviations; routine agreements may follow a shorter approved route.
GDPR applies to personal data exchanged during contracting; national rules govern relevant employment and consultation matters.
Build ranges cover one contract family and include access, legal template review, and applicable employee consultation.
unknowns: Does the role negotiate external client contracts or only internal training agreements?
Which commitments can the specialist make without further approval?
Are approved clauses and pricing rules maintained?
Can the {CLM} and {ESIGN} preserve structured contract fields?
Which employee consultation and access procedures apply under national rules?
research_questions: How much contract wording is genuinely bespoke after templates are standardised?
Can obligations be transferred from approved structured fields without interpreting signed documents?
new_work: Review generated scope wording and detect commitments beyond the brief.
Maintain approved rates, clauses, and delegation limits.
Resolve contract-version mismatches and failed obligation transfers.
Check that registered billing and delivery details match the signed agreement.

role.altitude: The week shifts from gathering records, chasing placements, and preparing paperwork toward access conversations, teaching fit, programme choices, and negotiation. Existing approval rights remain; better preparation supports more frequent programme recommendations.
reach: Help Training and Development Managers choose module refreshes and protect critical instructor coverage.
Help Human Resources Specialists investigate barriers to development access.
Help Human Resources Managers assess training commitments and measurable outcomes.
skills_to_grow: Translate learning needs into structured briefs and measurable outcomes.
Define scheduling constraints without hiding unfair allocation choices.
Check generated text against sources and contractual limits.
Assess teaching fit and facilitate difficult access conversations.
Understand GDPR, relevant EU AI Act uses, and employee consultation under national rules.
Maintain data definitions and diagnose workflow exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: Use dependable administration to offer shift-compatible training, maintain backup instructor coverage, and bring monthly module-refresh decisions supported by operational evidence.
